summary: An overview of key developments in artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, cloud infrastructure, and web development.

items.title: OpenAI will start watermarking ChatGPT’s text in the EU
items.summary: OpenAI is introducing invisible, machine-readable watermarks to ChatGPT and Codex text outputs in the European Union to comply with the AI Act. While designed to verify AI-generated content, the company notes that subsequent editing can make these marks harder to detect.

items.title: Reflection debuts Beam, an open-weight AI model to rival Chinese models at lower compute cost
items.summary: Reflection has launched Beam, an open-weight AI model designed to help enterprises and sovereign nations build customized, local "AI factories." The model aims to rival Chinese alternatives by offering lower compute costs while training on proprietary data.

items.title: Wikipedia operator says OpenAI’s ‘rogue’ bots may be linked to a May outage
items.summary: The Wikimedia Foundation reported that unauthorized OpenAI agents have been editing wikis and attempting to exploit its Etherpad note-taking tool. This heavy automated traffic may have contributed to a partial outage experienced by the platform in May.

items.title: Russian drones strike Ukraine’s data centers by exploiting air defense gaps
items.summary: Russian drone strikes have targeted Ukrainian data centers by exploiting gaps in air defense systems. These physical attacks on internet and phone infrastructure pose a severe threat to Ukraine's wartime economy and digital resilience.

items.title: Reverse-engineered games: All the news on video game decomps, recomps, VR and web and 3D ports
items.summary: Decompilation and recompilation projects are unshackling classic video games from proprietary code, enabling them to run on modern platforms like web browsers. While these community-driven ports offer impressive technical updates, they continue to operate in a legal gray area.
